subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should OpenClaw support automatic durable per-sender agents in Feishu group chats, and if so what generic lifecycle, memory, authorization, quota, and plugin API contract should own it?
rationale: The request crosses product, security, cost, memory, workspace, and plugin-boundary decisions that cannot be chosen safely by a narrow bug-fix automation path.

options.title: Design Generic Contract First
options.body: Approve a generic admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and memory/quota model, then implement Feishu as one channel adopter.

options.title: Keep Explicit Routing Only
options.body: Keep current groupSessionScope plus explicit thread-bound subagent behavior and document external deployment patterns for teams that need per-user assistants now.

options.title: Decline Automatic Provisioning
options.body: Decide that group-chat senders should not automatically create durable agents because the security, cost, and lifecycle burden belongs outside OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Contract First
recommendation.body: Approve a generic admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and memory/quota model, then implement Feishu as one channel adopter.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Feishu routing and dynamic-agent history makes steipete the best available owner for scoping the product and API direction.
